title: Google has promised to pay $44bn of rent on buildings it will never own

content_html:
Start with the number, because the number moved fast.

Google has agreed to cover as much as $44bn of lease payments on data centres owned by other people, should the tenant default. It disclosed the figure last week. At the end of September the same commitment stood at $6.5bn, The Information reported.

That is close to seven times larger in nine months.

The promise is simple to state and hard to price. Google does not own the building. It does not occupy the building. It has told the lenders that if the company renting the building stops paying, Google will.

Why a search company is underwriting other people’s rent

The answer is chips. Google wants customers for its tensor processing units, the in-house silicon it is pitching as an alternative to Nvidia.

A guarantee from a company with Google’s balance sheet lets a data-centre developer borrow more cheaply. Cheaper debt makes the project work. The project buys TPUs. Anthropic rents them.

Readers here have seen the mechanism. In June we reported how Google borrowed Nvidia’s own playbook, including a $3.2bn guarantee at Lake Mariner in western New York, $7bn at River Bend in Louisiana and $1.4bn in Texas.

What is new is the total, and the speed. Those individual guarantees have now consolidated into a single disclosed figure that has grown almost sevenfold since September.

A different kind of balance sheet

Until a year or two ago the giants had simple accounts. Cash covered debt several times over. That is no longer the shape of the thing.

Now they use techniques long familiar on Wall Street, expanding the business without carrying all of the risk themselves. The guarantee is the purest example. It commits nothing today and everything in the wrong scenario.

We have covered the aggregate before. Five US giants carry $1.65tn of off-balance-sheet AI debt, more than they report outright. This is the same story told through one company and one line item.

The machinery, and why it is legal

Moody’s set out the mechanics earlier this year. The five biggest US hyperscalers had amassed $969bn of future lease commitments by the end of 2025. Some $662bn of that had not yet commenced, so none of it sat on a balance sheet, Fortune reported. That hidden portion equals 113% of the five firms’ adjusted debt.

The cause is the kit. Data-centre leases used to run 10 to 15 years. AI hardware is useful for four to six. So tenants now demand short leases with options to renew, and landlords demand security before they will build.

The security is usually a residual value guarantee. If the tenant walks away and the building is worth less than an agreed threshold, the tenant pays the difference.

Accounting rules let that sit off the books. A renewal counts as a liability only if it is “reasonably certain”, a test above 70%. Since nobody can say what AI hardware will need in 2031, firms can argue the renewal is likely without being certain, and the guarantee stays in a footnote.

Meta shows the scale. It disclosed data-centre leases starting in 2029 worth about $12.3bn, alongside a residual value guarantee with a $28bn threshold. It judged a payout not probable, so no liability was recorded. Its $50bn Hyperion campus in Louisiana runs on a version of the same structure.

‘Every nook and cranny’

The reason for all this creativity is that the money required has outgrown the ordinary ways of raising it.

John Greenwood, Goldman Sachs’s global head of infrastructure and real asset finance, said he is “looking for capital in every nook and cranny” to support an expected $7.5tn of spending on chips, data centres and power over the next five years, The Information reported.

The hunt does not stop there. Much of that spending goes on chips that need replacing every few years, so the bill arrives again.

The thing money cannot buy quickly

Capital is not the only bottleneck. Nvidia says the harder constraint is physical.

“What’s limiting the access to compute capacity is the fact that it’s very hard to find powered data centers, powered land,” said Raj Mirpuri, Nvidia’s vice president of global AI clouds and infrastructure.

That is why the guarantees exist. A promise from a trillion-dollar balance sheet is the fastest way to turn a plot of land with a grid connection into a building full of chips. Nvidia is now doing the same thing, using its own balance sheet to help customers afford chips and help partners finance the halls to put them in.

Why it matters on Wednesday

Meta and Microsoft report on Wednesday. Amazon and Apple follow on Thursday. Alphabet went first last week and lifted its capital-expenditure guidance to $205bn.

The reported debt will look manageable. The guarantees will not be in the headline numbers.

Investors are already uneasy. Meta is down about 10% this year and Microsoft about 21%, while Apple, which barely spends on AI, is up 23%. Microsoft is short of compute and rationing it. Amazon has guided to roughly $200bn of capital spending against about $185bn of expected operating cash flow, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence, which means dipping into reserves it has topped up with bond sales.

It is in talks to backstop about $250bn of OpenAI’s financing, and it just put $1bn into Korea’s Naver alongside $9bn from Brookfield. The guarantee has become standard equipment.

None of it is improper. The disclosures exist. Moody’s analysts David Gonzales and Alastair Drake made the narrower point that these obligations are not missing, only early. They have not yet been triggered, but they will be.

Their warning was about what the accounts cannot show. “The accounting liability is unlikely to reflect certain plausible future scenarios,” they wrote.

A guarantee costs nothing at all, right up until the moment it costs everything. Google has written $44bn of them in nine months, on buildings it will never own.

Amazon has guided to roughly $200bn of capital spending against about $185bn of expected operating cash flow, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence, which means dipping into reserves it has topped up with bond sales.

content_html_zh:
从数字开始，因为数字移动得很快。

如果租户违约，谷歌已同意为其他人拥有的数据中心支付高达 440 亿美元的租金。 它上周披露了这一数字。 据 The Information 报道，截至 9 月底，承诺金额为 65 亿美元。

九个月内这个数字几乎增加了七倍。

这种承诺说起来很简单，但很难定价。 谷歌并不拥有该大楼。 它不占用建筑物。 它告诉贷方，如果租赁该大楼的公司停止付款，谷歌将停止付款。

为什么搜索公司要承保其他人的租金

答案是芯片。 谷歌希望为其张量处理单元赢得客户，谷歌将这种内部芯片作为英伟达的替代品。

拥有谷歌资产负债表的公司提供的担保可以让数据中心开发商以更便宜的价格借款。 更便宜的债务使该项目得以实施。 该项目购买 TPU。 人类租用它们。

读者在这里已经看到了这个机制。 6 月，我们报道了谷歌如何借用 Nvidia 自己的剧本，包括在纽约西部的 Lake Mariner 提供 32 亿美元的担保，在路易斯安那州的 River Bend 提供 70 亿美元的担保，以及在德克萨斯州提供 14 亿美元的担保。

新的是总量和速度。 这些个人担保现已合并为一个披露的数字，自 9 月份以来该数字几乎增长了七倍。

不同类型的资产负债表

直到一两年前，这些巨头的账目还很简单。 现金弥补了债务好几倍。 那不再是事物的形状了。

现在，他们使用华尔街早已熟悉的技术来扩大业务，而无需自己承担所有风险。 保证就是最纯粹的例子。 今天它什么也没做，而且一切都是在错误的情况下发生的。

我们之前已经介绍过聚合。 五家美国巨头背负着 1.65 万亿美元的表外人工智能债务，比他们直接报告的还要多。 这是通过一家公司和一个订单项讲述的同一个故事。

机器及其合法性

穆迪今年早些时候制定了相关机制。 到 2025 年底，美国最大的五家超大规模企业已积累了 9690 亿美元的未来租赁承诺。 据《财富》杂志报道，其中约 6,620 亿美元尚未开始，因此资产负债表上没有任何资金。 该隐藏部分相当于五家公司调整后债务的 113%。

原因就出在套件上。 数据中心的租赁期限过去为 10 至 15 年。 人工智能硬件对四到六个人有用。 因此，租户现在要求短期租约并可以续约，而房东则要求在建造之前有安全保障。

担保通常是残值保证。 如果租户离开并且建筑物的价值低于约定的阈值，则租户需要支付差额。

会计规则不允许这种情况出现在账簿上。 仅当“相当确定”（测试结果高于 70%）时，续约才算作负债。 由于没有人能说出 2031 年人工智能硬件将需要什么，因此公司可以在不确定的情况下辩称更新是可能的，并且保证保留在脚注中。

元显示了规模。 它披露了从 2029 年开始的价值约 123 亿美元的数据中心租赁，以及门槛为 280 亿美元的剩余价值担保。 它判断不可能支付，因此没有记录任何责任。 位于路易斯安那州、耗资 500 亿美元的海伯利安园区采用的是同一结构的一个版本。

“每个角落和缝隙”

所有这些创造力的原因是所需的资金已经超出了常规的筹集资金的方式。

据 The Information 报道，高盛全球基础设施和实物资产融资主管约翰·格林伍德 (John Greenwood) 表示，他正在“在各个角落寻找资本”，以支持未来五年预计在芯片、数据中心和电力方面的 7.5 万亿美元支出。

狩猎并没有就此停止。 大部分支出都花在了每隔几年就需要更换的芯片上，因此账单又来了。

金钱无法快速买到的东西

资金并不是唯一的瓶颈。 英伟达表示，更严格的限制是物理上的。

英伟达全球人工智能云和基础设施副总裁 Raj Mirpuri 表示：“限制计算能力的原因是很难找到供电数据中心、供电土地。”

这就是保证存在的原因。 万亿美元资产负债表的承诺是将一块带有电网连接的土地变成一座充满芯片的建筑的最快方法。 英伟达现在也在做同样的事情，利用自己的资产负债表帮助客户购买芯片，并帮助合作伙伴为安装芯片的大厅提供资金。

为什么周三很重要

Meta 和微软周三发布报告。 亚马逊和苹果周四紧随其后。 Alphabet 上周率先将资本支出指引上调至 2050 亿美元。

报告的债务看起来是可控的。 这些保证不会出现在标题数字中。

投资者已经感到不安。 Meta 今年下跌了约 10%，微软下跌了约 21%，而几乎没有在 AI 上投入的苹果却上涨了 23%。 微软缺乏计算能力并对其进行配给。 根据标准普尔全球市场情报公司的数据，亚马逊指导了约 2000 亿美元的资本支出，而预期运营现金流约为 1850 亿美元，这意味着动用其通过债券销售补充的储备。

该公司正在就支持 OpenAI 约 2500 亿美元的融资进行谈判，并且刚刚向韩国 Naver 投资了 10 亿美元，同时还向 Brookfield 投资了 90 亿美元。 该保证已成为标准装备。

没有一个是不合适的。 这些披露是存在的。 穆迪分析师戴维·冈萨雷斯（David Gonzales）和阿拉斯泰尔·德雷克（Alastair Drake）提出了更狭隘的观点，即这些义务并没有缺失，只是过早。 它们尚未被触发，但它们将会被触发。

他们的警告是关于账户无法显示的内容。 他们写道：“会计负债不太可能反映某些可能的未来情景。”

担保根本不需要任何成本，直到它付出一切的那一刻。 谷歌在 9 个月内已为它永远不会拥有的建筑物写下了 440 亿美元的资金。
